newsitem.title: CHINA: China to hold first nuclear accident exercise.
newsitem.headline: China to hold first nuclear accident exercise.

text.p: China plans to stage its first drill to test its nuclear emergency response system and practise handling a potential nuclear disaster, the official China Daily said on Saturday.
The announcement follows an accident at a Japanese nuclear waste reprocessing plant last month that exposed 37 workers to low-level radiation in Japan's worst-ever nuclear mishap.
Such accidents should never happen in China, the newspaper quoted Ye Qing, executive vice-minister of the State Planning Commission, as saying.
The National Nuclear Emergency Coordination Committee would help organise the drill, which would be held at a nuclear power station at the end of this year or early next year, the newspaper said.

Central and local authorities would also set up emergency funds to help deal with any future nuclear accident, and Beijing would draw up an agenda for implementing a national plan for dealing with such an accident, it said.

Officials from China's two nuclear power plants, in Guangdong province's Daya Bay near Hong Kong and in Qinshan in eastern Zhejiang province, said the stations had been operating safely, the newspaper said.
China had plans to build four more nuclear power plants with a combined capacity of 6,500 megawatts, it said. Nuclear power accounts for one percent of China's total energy generation.
